claims.paraphrase: Page title.
The seam detects entries a deploy carried across their first publish, for the site to fan out.
The engine sends nothing over the network; it only ships the diffing logic.
Section heading.
buildNewlyPublished diffs two manifests down to first-publish transitions.
Snippet: parse both manifests from the delivery data subpath and loop over the newly published entries.
An entry is newly published when live, stamped in after, and unstamped or absent in before.
A carried stamp or a live entry never stamped does not match.
The draft check runs first and excludes a draft whether or not its stamp changed.
A removal is silent here because an entry deleted from after never comes back.
The helper is pure: no I/O and no clock read, so results are deterministic.
Section heading.
The engine keeps no state across deploys.
A null before means no prior manifest and returns every stamped live entry, a full fan-out.
A full fan-out suits a first backfill run, not an ordinary deploy.
The site persists the prior manifest between deploys and passes it as before.
Section heading.
A rename changes the concept and id identity key, so it reads as a new publish.
The helper cannot tell a renamed entry from a new one; a site must filter renames itself.
Section heading.
Deleting a published entry and recreating one under the same id re-announces it as a first publish.
A row keeps its stamp only while it exists and stays published.
Section heading.
A fresh publish appears once and not again on a later unchanged deploy.
A rename shows up too unless the site filters it.
A deletion never shows up.
